newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - March 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - March 26.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- Labor unions for city bus drivers in Seoul and five major cities decided to go on strike starting Wednesday
- South Korea Parliament Speaker Kim Soo-han suggested to President Kim Young-sam a cabinet system to replace the current presidential system

- Bank of Korea tries to keep won-dollar rate below 900: the won fell for the seventh consecutive day, briefly hitting 888.80 the lowest level in 10 years and nine months, as companies rushed to by dollars to prepare for the settlement of payments.
- Seoul City Hall decided to raise bus fares by 10 percent to 440 won begining sometime next month.
- The government plans to set next year's budget at 78 trillion won, up 9 percent compared to this year's 71 trillion won and the lowest increase in 14 years.

- Visiting U.S. House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich yesterday pledged to do his best to enact a pilot visa waiver program for Koreas during the forthcoming spring Congressional session, Foreign Minister officals said.

- The prosecution, expanding a reinvestigation of the loans-for-kickbacks scandal of the Hanbo Group, is calling for a joint investigation of the scandal along with the Board of Audit and Inspection and other government agencies.

- South Korea ranked 31st among 46 countries in terms of state competitiveness this year, a sharp drop from 27th in 1996 and 25th in 1995, the International Institute for Management Development in Switzerland recently said.
